steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Spray a 9x5-inch loaf pan with cooking spray, or line with parchment paper.
Sprinkle plums with 1 tablespoon of flour in a medium bowl; toss to coat. Set aside.

Beat white sugar, butter, and vanilla extract in a large bowl with an electric mixer until light and fluffy; beat in eggs. Sift 1 1/2 cups flour, salt, and baking soda into a separate bowl. Stir into sugar-egg mixture, alternating with yogurt until smooth. Fold in plums. Pour batter into the prepared loaf pan. Sprinkle brown sugar on top.

Bake in the preheated oven until a toothpick inserted into center of loaf comes out clean, 45 to 50 minutes. Remove from oven; let cool in the pan for 15 minutes before inverting onto a wire rack to cool completely.

raw_recipe.headline: My Mother-in-Law's Plum Bread
raw_recipe.description: My mother-in-law's plum bread recipe makes a sweet loaf with fresh, chopped plums, yogurt, and other simple ingredients for deliciously moist results.
raw_recipe.name: My Mother-in-Law's Plum Bread

review.reviewBody: Just made 2 loaves. Added 1/2 c more of the plums and I didn't have yogurt so I used sour cream , used 1/3 c butter. I added in 1/2 tsp of orange extract also. Very yummy!! Thanks for sharing

After reading other reviews, I took some of the suggestions, and added 1/3 cup chopped pecans, 1 teasp Cinnamon, 1/2 teas almond extract, and some grated orange rind. I used unsalted butter instead of margarine, and tried to control the calories a bit by substituting granulated Splenda for sugar. I decided to make muffins instead of bread, and I used non-stick silicone muffin liners to avoid sticking. I increased the plums to 1 1/2 cups (because I had 30 lbs of plums.) Baking took 30 minutes, and the recipe made 16 small muffins with 190 calories each. They were delicious and very moist. I will have to dole them out carefully to my husband, or they will all be gone in a flash.

Very moist!! I used vanilla yogurt because that is what I had and exactly 1 cup of peeled, diced plums. Added a dash of cinnamon and a few pieces of pecans on top. I used 1/2 tsp of baking soda. They rose beautifully. This recipe made enough for 4 mini loaves. In my Emeril oven on the bake setting at 375F they took 20 minutes to cook. Perfect for summer when you don’t need a hot kitchen!

Changed it up abit to cut sugar, sodium and fat. I used 1 c. frozen plums cut up ( not drained), 1/3 c raisins with the 1 Tbsp. flour and for Wet Ingredients used 2 eggs, 1/3 c oil, 1/3 c brown sugar, ( will use honey next time), vanilla. For Dry , I used 1 c. all purp flour and 1/2 whole wheat, 1 tsp b. powder, 1/4 b. soda. I used 1/3 c vanilla yogurt, topped off the loaf with walnuts, and baked in my toaster oven covering it for last minutes. I found my loaf really moist , maybe too moist , so will cut by 1 egg. or drain my frozen plums. I love it and sweet enough for me.

Made 2 loaves with white sugar for 1 loaf (i.e. it was cut in half). Used butter instead of margarine, and used over 1.5 cups of plums per loaf (so over 3 cups of plums for 2 loaves). Baked 2 loaves for 1 hour.
It turned out great.
Super easy recipe that I would definitely use again (and *soon* as I can make more bread to give away with the extra plums from my tree, now that I know that the recipe is good).
Thank you for this!

Ok, so I had to change a few things. Baking for a diabetic can be a challenge. I cut the white sugar to 1/4 cup, the rest, Splenda. I used a scant 1/2 of it due to reviews saying it was a bit sweet. Increased the plums by 1/2 cup. Doubled the vanilla, and soda. Sour cream instead of yogurt. I didn't have any. Topped with chopped pecans and dusted top with Splenda brown sugar. My husband went wild!!! So good. I'm sure the original recipe would be just as wonderful. I just wanted to let those bakers know that substituting spoonable Splenda works well for this wonderful cake.

I did, for the second loaf, substitute 1/3cup brown sugar for granulated. I also was on ginger kick or binge so added approximately 1/4tsp of finely minced peeled fresh ginger and about the same amount of candied ginger I recently made - also minced finely. One person who tried it asked, in an almost accusatory tone - demanded, really, "Why have I never had this before?" Meaning he quite liked it. And I almost forgot the most important change: I use Italian prune plums, chopped fresh and then stored in my freezer. My friends who have had any are huge fans. Me too, by the way.

Absolutely loved it. I used wild plums picked on our place on the Yellowstone river (Montana) I used a little bit more plums than called for and also more vanilla and baking soda. Yogurt used was honey vanilla flavor greek yogurt (Greek Godz brand). SOOOOO good that I am sitting her cutting up more wild plums to make more bread to freeze.

Excellent as written. my plums were overly ripe, soft and juicy, so "tossing" them with flour just would have made a paste, so I skipped that part. I did have to bake it 15 more minutes than the recipe said, but it came out great and looking like the photo. I had more plums, so decided to make another batch; however, I had used up all the yogurt. Added some leftover almond paste I had in the fridge, with a splash of amaretto instead of vanilla. I also put the plums in earlier. Since they were so soft, they disappeared into the batter. That loaf came out not so moist, and without the obvious chunks of plum, but still very good.

Love this recipe. Made it over the summer with my plums which were slightly tart, added 1/2 cup chopped walnuts and used vanilla greek yogurt instead of plain. Fantastic! Made a variation for Christmas where I replaced the plums with 1/2 cup each chopped apples and cranberries. Again, so yummy!

Loved it - great crunchy top, light and tasty. I used 1 1/2 slightly heaped cups of plums. 1/2 tsp baking soda as some suggested and I added 1/4 tsp cinnamon (Vietnamese Penzy brand). I only had coconut yogurt which is runnier so it took much longer to bake so will use thicker Greek yogurt next time. Excellent though and not overly sweet!
I added more fruit than recommended. The recipe is easy to follow. The yogurt & butter together makes a almost pound cake texture. I am on my 3rd loaf. I highly recommend this recipe. 👍
I loved this recipe. My blackberries are ripening so I added them to half the plums. Definitely a keep and I’ll make it again. Thanks for sharing

I’ve made it three times, each with a different fruit: plums, apricots and strawberries. Planning to use blueberries next, then blackberries. The texture of the bread itself is very nice, a little dense, which holds the fruit pretty well. I refrigerate when cooled, eases slicing. The brown sugar topping adds a lot! Yum!
Very good, I used butter instead of margarine, and 1/2C more of plums and 1/2C of rcushed Almonds and taste was heavenly.
Keeper recipe! I doubled vanilla and baking soda, halfed the white sugar. It's moist, sweet and a bit tart with the sugar cut down, SO tasty!
Tasty recipe. I made a double recipe with butter and sour cream as they were on hand. I also omitted about a half cup of the sugar and I only used 1/8 cup of brown sugar for the topping on each loaf.
Excellent recipe! I used 1.5 cups of plums and it was just right. The sugar sprinkled on the top is a great idea.
